questions.q: The market for piped water in a Nigerian state is served by one firm because duplicating the pipe network would make production wasteful. This situation is best described as
questions.explanation: A natural monopoly arises when one firm can supply the whole market at a lower average cost because of economies of scale, as with a piped-water network. It is not chiefly created by law, and with one supplier the market is neither oligopolistic nor perfectly competitive.

questions.q: Kola and three other firms in a Nigerian town sell almost identical sachet water, and each firm considers the likely reactions of the others before changing its price. The market structure is
questions.explanation: An oligopoly has few sellers whose decisions are interdependent, so a price change by one firm affects and invites responses from the others. Perfect competition has many price-taking sellers, while monopoly has a single seller.

questions.q: A firm under perfect competition in Jos produces at an output where price is ₦80, marginal cost is ₦80 and average cost is ₦72. In the short run, the firm should
options: shut down immediately because average cost is below price
raise its price above ₦80 to cover costs
reduce output so that marginal cost falls below price
continue producing at the current output and earn supernormal profit
questions.explanation: Under perfect competition, price equals marginal revenue, so price = marginal cost at the current output means the firm is maximizing profit. Since price also exceeds average cost, it earns supernormal profit; it cannot set a higher price as a price taker.

questions.q: The price of a piece of ankara fabric in Onitsha falls from ₦4,000 to ₦3,600, and the quantity demanded per week rises from 100 to 130 pieces. Calculate the price elasticity of demand, using the initial values as base and ignoring the negative sign.
questions.explanation: Using initial values, the percentage change in quantity is (30 ÷ 100) × 100 = 30%, and the percentage change in price is (400 ÷ 4,000) × 100 = 10%. Dividing 30% by 10% gives a price elasticity of 3.0, so demand is elastic. A value such as 0.33 comes from inverting the correct ratio or using the wrong base.

questions.q: Which of the following will most likely make the demand for a particular brand of sachet water in Enugu more price elastic?
options: The brand is regarded as an essential item with no close substitute
Consumers spend a very small fraction of their income on the brand
The existence of many close substitute brands
Consumers have a very short period in which to adjust their purchases
questions.explanation: Demand is more elastic when close substitutes are readily available, because buyers can switch brands when the price rises. Necessity, a small share of income and a short adjustment period tend to make demand less elastic, not more elastic.

questions.q: The Enugu State government imposes a unit tax on a soft drink whose demand is highly inelastic while supply is relatively elastic. Who will bear the larger share of the tax?
options: Producers, because supply is relatively elastic
Consumers and producers equally, because the tax is imposed by government
Producers, because demand is highly inelastic
Consumers, because quantity demanded changes little when price rises
questions.explanation: The tax burden falls more heavily on the side of the market that is less able to change quantity, which here is consumers with highly inelastic demand. With relatively elastic supply, producers can reduce quantity supplied more easily, so they can pass more of the tax forward to consumers.

questions.q: Which statement best distinguishes economic development from economic growth?
options: Economic development includes a sustained rise in real income together with improved welfare and structural change, while economic growth is simply an increase in real output.
Economic growth includes improved health and education, while economic development is only a rise in national income.
Economic development is measured only by increases in real GDP, while economic growth includes income distribution.
Economic growth and economic development mean the same thing when population is constant.
questions.explanation: Economic growth refers mainly to an increase in real output or real income, whereas development also involves qualitative improvements such as better health, education, reduced inequality and structural change. Treating the two as identical ignores the welfare and distributional aspects of development.

questions.q: A national development plan that is reviewed annually and extended by one year so that it always covers a fixed number of years ahead is known as a
questions.explanation: A rolling plan is revised each year and extended by another year, so the plan period keeps moving forward over a constant horizon. A fixed-term plan covers a set period without annual extension, while perspective planning sets long-term goals and project appraisal assesses specific projects.

questions.q: In a given year, a country's export price index is 150 and its import price index is 120. Using the ratio of export prices to import prices, calculate the country's terms of trade.
questions.explanation: The terms of trade are calculated as (export price index ÷ import price index) × 100, giving (150 ÷ 120) × 100 = 125. A value above 100 indicates favourable terms of trade, while 80 would result from inverting the ratio.

questions.q: The Nigerian government introduces an import quota on frozen fish. Which of the following is a direct expected effect of this quota?
options: The government collects a fixed tariff revenue on each unit of frozen fish imported.
Domestic consumers pay lower prices immediately because imports are restricted.
The quantity of imported frozen fish allowed into the country is limited, tending to raise the domestic price.
Foreign suppliers face no restriction and therefore compete more freely in the Nigerian market.
questions.explanation: An import quota directly restricts the maximum quantity that may be imported, reducing supply and generally raising the domestic price. A tariff raises revenue per unit, but a quota works mainly by limiting quantity rather than by collecting a fixed amount on each unit.

questions.q: The body responsible for regulating and developing the Nigerian capital market is the
questions.explanation: The Securities and Exchange Commission is the apex regulatory body for Nigeria’s capital market. The Central Bank of Nigeria supervises banks and monetary policy, while the Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation insures deposits and the National Insurance Commission regulates insurance.

questions.q: A company in Ibadan sells shares to the public for the first time to raise long-term capital. This sale takes place in the
questions.explanation: A first-time sale of new shares to raise long-term capital is made in the primary market. The secondary market deals in existing securities, while the money market handles short-term funds and the foreign exchange market deals in currencies.

questions.q: Ngozi instructs her bank to pay ₦25,000 every month to her landlord from her salary account. This banking instruction is a
questions.explanation: A standing order is the customer’s instruction to the bank to pay a fixed amount at regular intervals. A direct debit is initiated by the creditor, an overdraft is a borrowing facility, and a credit transfer is a general transfer rather than a regular fixed instruction.

questions.q: A small bakery in Ilorin employs four workers and produces 100 loaves of bread per day. When a fifth worker is employed, total output rises to 112 loaves per day. The marginal product of the fifth worker is
questions.explanation: Marginal product is the change in total output when one more worker is employed. Here, output rises from 100 to 112 loaves, so the marginal product is 112 - 100 = 12 loaves per day.

questions.q: Which of the following is a fixed cost for a printing press in the short run?
options: Cost of paper used for printing
Cost of ink used in printing
Rent paid on the factory building
questions.explanation: A fixed cost does not change with the level of output in the short run. Factory rent must be paid whether more or fewer print jobs are handled, while ink, casual wages and paper vary with output.

questions.q: A firm’s total fixed cost is ₦2,000 and its total variable cost at 10 units of output is ₦3,000. What is its average total cost at 10 units?
questions.explanation: Total cost is total fixed cost plus total variable cost: ₦2,000 + ₦3,000 = ₦5,000. Average total cost is ₦5,000 ÷ 10 = ₦500.

questions.q: A worker earns ₦180,000 per month when the price index is 150. If the price index rises to 180, by how much does the real value of the salary fall per month?
A sustained fall in the general price level of goods and services is called
questions.explanation: Deflation is a sustained fall in the general price level. Disinflation refers to a fall in the rate of inflation, stagflation combines inflation with stagnation, and reflation is a deliberate policy to raise prices after a fall.

questions.q: An outward shift of a country's production possibility frontier is most likely caused by
options: an increase in consumers' demand for one good
questions.explanation: An outward shift means the economy can produce more of both goods, usually because productive capacity has increased. Improved technology raises efficiency, while unemployment and inefficiency keep production inside the frontier and higher demand alone does not shift the frontier.

questions.q: Which of the following would shift the supply curve of garri to the right?
options: an increase in the market price of garri
an increase in the wages of garri producers
the introduction of a more efficient cassava-processing machine
questions.explanation: A rightward shift of supply means more garri is supplied at each price, often due to lower production costs or better technology. A more efficient processing machine does this; higher garri prices move along the supply curve, while higher wages and poor cassava harvests reduce supply.

questions.q: In Aba, the price of a close substitute for locally made palm oil falls. What is the most likely effect on the demand for palm oil?
options: The demand curve for palm oil shifts to the right.
The demand curve for palm oil shifts to the left.
The supply curve of palm oil shifts to the left.
There is a movement upward along the same demand curve for palm oil.
questions.explanation: A fall in the price of a substitute makes palm oil less attractive at every price, so its demand decreases and the demand curve shifts to the left. A movement along a demand curve is caused by a change in the good's own price, not by a change in the price of a substitute.

questions.q: A sachet-water producer in Akure has fixed cost of ₦45,000 per month. At an output of 15,000 bags, total variable cost is ₦90,000. Her average total cost per bag is
questions.explanation: Total cost is ₦45,000 + ₦90,000 = ₦135,000. Average total cost is ₦135,000 ÷ 15,000 = ₦9.00 per bag. The ₦3.00 and ₦6.00 values are the average fixed cost and average variable cost respectively, not the average total cost.

questions.q: A furniture maker in Ilorin has total revenue TR = 80Q − Q² and total cost TC = 200 + 20Q, where Q is the number of chairs. What is her profit when Q = 10?
questions.explanation: At Q = 10, TR = 80(10) − 10² = 800 − 100 = ₦700, while TC = 200 + 20(10) = ₦400. Profit is TR − TC = ₦700 − ₦400 = ₦300; ₦700 is total revenue, not profit.

questions.q: A firm has total fixed cost of ₦12,000. At an output of 200 units, its total cost is ₦32,000. What is its average variable cost?
questions.explanation: Total variable cost is total cost less total fixed cost: ₦32,000 − ₦12,000 = ₦20,000. Average variable cost is ₦20,000 ÷ 200 = ₦100 per unit. The ₦60 value is average fixed cost, while ₦160 is average total cost.

questions.q: The difference between Gross Domestic Product at market prices and Gross Domestic Product at factor cost is
questions.explanation: GDP at market prices includes indirect taxes and excludes subsidies, whereas GDP at factor cost records payments to factors of production. The difference is therefore indirect taxes minus subsidies, also called net indirect taxes.

questions.q: A country's nominal GDP rises from ₦80 billion to ₦96 billion while the GDP deflator rises from 100 to 120. The country's real GDP
questions.explanation: Real GDP = nominal GDP × 100 ÷ GDP deflator. Initially it is ₦80 billion × 100 ÷ 100 = ₦80 billion, and later it is ₦96 billion × 100 ÷ 120 = ₦80 billion. The rise in nominal GDP is fully offset by higher prices, so real GDP is unchanged.

questions.q: The Bank of Agriculture was established mainly to
options: regulate the quality of manufactured goods.
provide credit to farmers and other rural enterprises.
provide free storage facilities to manufacturing firms.
fix the producer prices of export crops.
questions.explanation: The Bank of Agriculture is primarily involved in agricultural and rural finance, especially providing credit for farming and related enterprises. Price fixing, storage provision for manufacturers, and quality regulation are handled by other institutions.

questions.q: A rice farmer in Kebbi harvested 8,000 kg of paddy rice. After milling, 5,600 kg of milled rice was obtained. The processing recovery rate is
questions.explanation: Processing recovery rate is (milled rice obtained ÷ paddy rice harvested) × 100 = (5,600 ÷ 8,000) × 100 = 70%. The remaining 30% represents loss or waste during processing, not the recovery rate.

questions.q: In a local government area in Osun State, 500,000 people are aged 15–64. Of these, 280,000 are employed and 20,000 are unemployed but actively looking for work. What is the labour force participation rate?
questions.explanation: The labour force is 280,000 + 20,000 = 300,000. The participation rate is (300,000 ÷ 500,000) × 100 = 60%. The value 56% is the employment rate, not the participation rate.

questions.q: During the dry season, many workers on a rice farm in Kebbi State are laid off because there is little work until the next planting season. The unemployment they experience is best described as
questions.explanation: Seasonal unemployment arises from regular changes in weather or production cycles, as in farming. It is not caused by a general economic downturn, a skills mismatch, or moving between jobs.

questions.q: A state government's budget includes the following items: salaries of civil servants, construction of a new market, purchase of tractors for mechanised farming, and repayment of the principal of a loan. Which item is classified as recurrent expenditure?
options: Repayment of the principal of a loan
Purchase of tractors for mechanised farming
questions.explanation: Recurrent expenditure covers day-to-day running costs such as salaries and wages. Construction, tractor purchase and loan principal repayment are capital items.

questions.q: A state government estimates total revenue of ₦72 billion and total expenditure of ₦84 billion for a coming year. How should the budget be described?
questions.explanation: A budget deficit occurs when expenditure exceeds revenue. Here the deficit is ₦84 billion − ₦72 billion = ₦12 billion. A surplus would arise if revenue were greater than expenditure.

questions.q: Which feature is most consistent with a perfectly competitive market?
options: A single firm controls the supply of the product
Each firm faces a downward-sloping demand curve
Each firm sells a product that is different from those of its rivals
Firms can enter and leave the industry without restriction
questions.explanation: Free entry and exit is a key condition for perfect competition. Differentiated products, a single controlling seller, and downward-sloping firm demand describe imperfectly competitive markets instead.

questions.q: A market is supplied by four large firms. Before changing its price, each firm tries to predict how the other three will react. This behaviour illustrates
questions.explanation: Mutual interdependence means each firm’s decisions depend on the expected reactions of rival firms, a key feature of oligopoly. Price discrimination and product differentiation are different pricing and product strategies.

questions.q: When the price of a bag of rice rises from ₦25,000 to ₦30,000, a household’s purchases fall from 8 bags to 6 bags a year. Using the initial values as the base and ignoring the negative sign, what is the price elasticity of demand?
questions.explanation: The price rise is (₦30,000 − ₦25,000) ÷ ₦25,000 × 100 = 20%. The quantity fall is (8 − 6) ÷ 8 × 100 = 25%, so elasticity is 25 ÷ 20 = 1.25. Demand is therefore elastic.

questions.q: Amina’s monthly income rises from ₦80,000 to ₦96,000, and the quantity of garri she buys falls from 30 kg to 24 kg. Using the initial values as the base, her income elasticity of demand for garri is
options: 0.2, and garri is a normal good
−0.2, and garri is an inferior good
−1.0, and garri is an inferior good
1.0, and garri is a normal good
questions.explanation: Income rises by (₦96,000 − ₦80,000) ÷ ₦80,000 × 100 = 20%, while quantity demanded changes by (24 − 30) ÷ 30 × 100 = −20%. Thus income elasticity is −20 ÷ 20 = −1.0. A negative income elasticity indicates an inferior good.

questions.q: In a village in Benue State, there are 1,200 children below 15 years, 3,000 persons aged 15–64, and 300 persons aged 65 years and above. What is the dependency ratio?
questions.explanation: The dependent population is 1,200 + 300 = 1,500, while the working-age population is 3,000. The dependency ratio is (1,500 ÷ 3,000) × 100 = 50 dependants per 100 working-age persons. Using only children gives 40 and ignores the elderly.

questions.q: A local government council in Ogun State receives money from fees paid by food vendors for health permits. In public finance, this receipt is best classified as
questions.explanation: Fees and charges paid for permits and services are non-tax revenue because they are not levied as taxes on income or goods. Direct and indirect taxes are compulsory tax receipts, while capital expenditure is a spending item.

questions.q: Which factor is a major constraint on the effective implementation of development plans in Nigeria?
options: Frequent changes in government and inadequate funding
Strict continuity of public projects across governments
questions.explanation: Development plans often fail when governments change and alter priorities or when funds are not released as planned. Adequate data, skilled planners and continuity of projects would support rather than constrain implementation.

questions.q: In development planning, a rolling plan is best described as a plan that
options: is revised annually while maintaining a constant planning horizon
depends entirely on foreign loans for its financing
is implemented only by local government councils
covers every sector of the economy in one year
questions.explanation: A rolling plan is reviewed and extended each year so that the planning period remains in view. It is not a one-year all-sector plan, nor is it limited to local governments or dependent entirely on foreign loans.

questions.q: Which of the following is an invisible export for Nigeria?
options: Earnings from foreigners who visit Calabar for tourism
Crude oil sold to a European refinery
questions.explanation: Tourism earnings from foreigners are payment for a service and are therefore an invisible export. Crude oil and cocoa are visible goods, while imported textiles are not exports at all.

questions.q: A major difference between an import quota and an import tariff is that an import quota
options: raises government revenue each time an imported unit enters
places a physical limit on the quantity of a good that may be imported
reduces the domestic price of the imported good
is imposed only on goods exported by a country
questions.explanation: A quota restricts imports directly by fixing the maximum quantity allowed, whereas a tariff is a tax on imports that raises their price. A quota does not automatically generate tariff revenue and is not imposed on exports.

questions.q: A short-term debt instrument issued by the Central Bank of Nigeria on behalf of the Federal Government is known as
questions.explanation: Treasury bills are short-term Federal Government securities usually issued for 91, 182 or 364 days through the Central Bank of Nigeria. Treasury bonds are longer-term government securities, while debentures and preference shares are corporate instruments.

questions.q: A bakery has total fixed cost of ₦6,000 and total variable cost of ₦14,000 when it produces 200 loaves of bread. Its average total cost per loaf is
questions.explanation: Total cost = ₦6,000 + ₦14,000 = ₦20,000. Average total cost = ₦20,000 ÷ 200 = ₦100 per loaf; ₦70 is the average variable cost, not the average total cost.

questions.q: During a period when Nigeria's money supply rises much faster than the volume of goods and services available, the quantity theory of money predicts that the most likely outcome is
options: an automatic increase in real output per worker
a reduction in the money value of goods and services
a persistent rise in the general price level
a proportional fall in the velocity of circulation
questions.explanation: According to the quantity theory, if money supply grows faster than real output while velocity is stable, the main effect is inflation. The equation MV = PY shows that a sustained rise in M relative to Y tends to raise P, the general price level.

questions.q: A commercial bank in Ibadan has excess reserves of ₦400,000. If the required cash reserve ratio is 20% and all the excess reserves are used for lending, what is the maximum possible expansion of bank deposits in the banking system? (Assume no cash leakage.)
questions.explanation: The maximum deposit expansion is found by multiplying excess reserves by the bank multiplier: ₦400,000 × (1 ÷ 0.20) = ₦2,000,000. Keeping only the original excess reserves would ignore the cumulative lending and redepositing process.

questions.q: A teacher's nominal monthly salary rises from ₦75,000 to ₦84,000 while the consumer price index rises by 8%. By approximately what percentage does the teacher's real salary change?
questions.explanation: The real salary is ₦84,000 ÷ 1.08 = ₦77,777.78. Compared with the original ₦75,000, this is a rise of about 3.7%. The nominal increase of 12% overstates the gain because prices rose by 8%.

questions.q: The demand for table salt in a typical household is likely to be price inelastic mainly because
options: salt is a luxury good with many close substitutes
the quantity of salt supplied is fixed in the short run
salt takes a large proportion of household income
salt has few close substitutes and takes a small share of the household budget
questions.explanation: Demand is price inelastic when consumers find few good substitutes and when the good takes only a small part of their budget. A change in the price of salt therefore causes only a small change in quantity demanded.

questions.q: A consumer buys and consumes successive bottles of soft drink. The additional satisfaction obtained from each extra bottle becomes smaller. This statement illustrates
options: the law of diminishing marginal utility
questions.explanation: Diminishing marginal utility states that as more units of a commodity are consumed, the extra satisfaction from each additional unit tends to fall. It describes consumption, not production returns or trade specialisation.

questions.q: The Anchor Borrowers' Programme of the Central Bank of Nigeria was introduced mainly to
options: fix the prices of imported manufactured goods
grant tax holidays to multinational oil companies
regulate interest rates charged by commercial banks
provide credit and inputs to smallholder farmers to increase production of staple crops
questions.explanation: The programme was designed to support smallholder farmers with credit and farm inputs so as to raise local production of staple crops and strengthen food security. It is not primarily a price-fixing, tax-holiday or interest-rate regulation scheme.
